hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with chest pain, hypotension, clear lung fields, elevated JVP, and Kussmaul's sign. ECG shows ST elevation in inferior leads (II, III, aVF) with ST elevation in V1 > V3 and ST elevation in V4R (right-sided leads) — indicating RV involvement. RV infarction occurs in ~30% of inferior MIs (usually RCA occlusion). RV is preload-dependent — nitroglycerin and morphine can cause dangerous hypotension because they reduce preload. Treatment: AVOID nitrates and diuretics (reduce preload → worsen RV output). Give IV fluids aggressively to maintain RV preload. Aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulation. REPERFUSION: emergent PCI (preferred) or fibrinolysis. If hypotensive despite fluids: dobutamine (inotrope). Atropine for bradycardia. Admit to CCU.
